notes: BACHELOR: no DAAD scholarship for foreign students to study for a full bachelor's degree in Germany was found. The DAAD overview page says its scholarships are 'aimed primarily at graduates, doctoral students and postdocs' and names master's, doctorate and postdoc only; the 'Important information for scholarship applicants' page funds Master's, doctoral and postdoc levels and mentions Bachelor's only as a prior qualification. The database landing page defines 'Graduates' as holders of a first degree. Recommend removing bachelor from the website entry.

Undergraduate-related database entries that exist but are NOT bachelor degree funding: (1) University Summer Courses (above, non-degree, bachelor's students need 2 years of study); (2) Gilman-DAAD Germany Scholarships (detail 57649740): for U.S. undergraduates (matriculated at a U.S. college, completed second year, Pell Grant recipients only) to study/intern in Germany for 1 to 12 months, a U.S.-only exchange not a bachelor's degree. Search results also showed database entries of other organisations (e.g. Friedrich Ebert Foundation, Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung) that include Bachelor's students already studying in Germany; these are third-party scholarships, not DAAD funding, and were not read in full.

Programme entries are DAAD scholarship lines, not named degree programmes; the database covers all subjects at German universities and is a search tool, so there is no fixed list. The STEM Master's line noted in the previous pass (developing and emerging countries) was not re-read in this pass.

Call details seen are for funding starting 2027; the lines read were closed or time-limited. The Master's page says applicants resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline are not considered.
